summary:
Junior Astronaut Training 🚀

Our project, Junior Astronaut Training, is an interactive learning platform designed to introduce students and young space enthusiasts to the exciting world of space exploration and astronaut training. We developed this project to make space education more engaging, accessible, and enjoyable through interactive activities, educational content, and astronaut-inspired challenges.

The project addresses the challenge of creating awareness and interest in space science by providing a virtual astronaut training experience. It helps young learners understand the skills, knowledge, physical fitness, and problem-solving abilities required to become an astronaut. Through engaging learning experiences, users can explore space-related concepts, test their knowledge, and develop curiosity about science and technology.

This project is important because many students dream of becoming astronauts but have limited opportunities to understand the actual training and challenges involved. Junior Astronaut Training bridges this gap by making space education accessible and inspiring the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space explorers.

Our vision is to transform learning into an exciting space adventure, encouraging young minds to dream big, think creatively, and explore beyond Earth.
details: Project ASTRA is an AI-powered Space Learning and Astronaut Training Academy designed to transform students' curiosity about space into practical knowledge and astronaut-style skills. It provides two age-based learning portals: Little Space Explorers for children under 12, featuring interactive lessons, educational games, planetary discovery, mini rocket missions, and a Digital Astronaut Passport; and Future Astronauts for learners aged 12 and above, offering advanced astronomy, physics, AI mentorship, rocket designing, orbital mechanics, and simulated Moon and Mars missions. The platform works through an interactive web-based environment where students learn concepts, complete missions, track their progress, earn experience points, and receive personalized AI guidance to identify knowledge gaps and improve their performance. It uses technologies such as React, Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Supabase/Firebase, Three.js, and AI assistance, along with NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day, Exoplanet Archive, NASA Eyes, and publicly available space datasets. Its major benefits include making space education engaging, accessible, interactive, and practical while developing scientific knowledge, critical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving skills. The intended impact is to inspire the next generation of scientists, researchers, and astronauts by providing a connected learning journey from basic astronomy to advanced space exploration. The creativity of ASTRA lies in combining AI-powered mentorship, gamification, digital astronaut passports, and realistic space mission simulations in one learning ecosystem. While designing the project, we considered affordability, accessibility across different age groups, ease of use, device compatibility, efficient resource usage, offline learning support, child safety, guardian consent, and data privacy to make space education more inclusive and effective.
